what_its_for: Hyoscyamine is used to treat stomach and intestinal problems such as cramps, spasms, and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). It helps reduce stomach acid and slows down the gut to relieve pain and discomfort. It may also be used to help dry up secretions before surgery, treat bladder problems, or manage other conditions your doctor has prescribed it for.
how_to_take: Take hyoscyamine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take the regular tablets or liquid by mouth with or without food. Let dissolving tablets (orally disintegrating tablets) melt on your tongue — do not chew or swallow them whole. Swallow extended-release capsules or tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. If you are using the liquid form, measure your dose carefully with a measuring spoon or syringe, not a kitchen spoon.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 0.125 mg to 0.25 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day, 30 to 60 minutes before meals and at bedtime, or as directed by your doctor. Extended-release forms are usually taken every 12 hours. Do not take more than 1.5 mg in a 24-hour period unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Doses for children are based on weight and age, so always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions carefully.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store hyoscyamine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking hyoscyamine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Be careful driving, operating machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated — hyoscyamine reduces sweating, which can make it easier to get heat stroke in hot weather. Avoid antacids within 1 hour of taking hyoscyamine, as they can make it less effective. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, especially antihistamines, sleep aids, or other stomach medications, as they can interact with hyoscyamine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: fast or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, confusion or hallucinations, difficulty urinating or no urination at all, severe constipation, eye pain or vision changes, fever with no sweating, skin rash or allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or if your symptoms get worse instead of better. Contact your doctor if you have dry mouth, blurred vision, or drowsiness that bothers you, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
when_it_works: Hyoscyamine usually starts working within 20 to 30 minutes after you take the regular tablet or liquid form. Extended-release forms work more slowly but last longer, typically 8 to 12 hours. You may notice relief from stomach cramping and spasms fairly quickly. If you do not notice any improvement after a few days, let your doctor know.
special_populations: Older adults (over 65): Use with extra caution. Elderly patients are more sensitive to the side effects of hyoscyamine, especially confusion, memory problems, urinary retention, and constipation. Lower doses are often recommended. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using hyoscyamine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is generally not recommended during pregnancy unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk. Breastfeeding: Hyoscyamine passes into breast milk and may reduce milk production. It is not recommended while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor about your options. Children: Dosing in children is based on weight. Be very careful to give the correct dose. This medication can cause serious side effects in children if too much is given. Patients with certain conditions: Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, enlarged prostate, urinary problems, heart disease, liver or kidney disease, or myasthenia gravis, as hyoscyamine may not be safe for you.
